item.title: SNAPSHOT | Wrexham prepare for Chelsea’s visit to the STōK Cae Ras
item.description: Wrexham AFC’s attention turns to FA Cup action as Chelsea head to the STōK Cae Ras for their first competitive match with the Red Dragons since February 1982. Wrexham’s sixth appearance in the fifth round and a first since 1997 sees Phil Parkinson’s side go head-to-head with a team placed fifth in the Premier League. item.title: COMMUNITY | Wrexham AFC Foundation deliver first-ever Street Dragons session in partnership with Llandudno FC
item.description: Wrexham AFC Foundation delivered its first-ever Street Dragons session outside of Wrexham during the February half-term, hosting a successful event in partnership with Llandudno FC. Held at Ty Llywellyn, Llandudno, the session was delivered as part of the Foundation’s funding from the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner for North Wales. item.title: FIXTURE NEWS | Swansea City vs Wrexham AFC Women rearranged fixture confirmed
item.description: After the postponement of Wrexham AFC Women’s Genero Premier Fixture against Swansea City last month, fixture details have now been confirmed for the rearranged fixture. The fixture will now take place on Wednesday, March 25 at 7:30pm. In addition to this, the match will be played at Cambrian United's ground, The M&P 3G, CF40 2XX. All tickets will be sold via the home club, with details announced in due course.

item.title: TICKET NEWS | Sheffield United (A) on sale from Monday at 10am
item.description: Tickets for our away fixture against Sheffield United on Saturday March 21, will go on sale to supporters from Monday March 9. item.title: CLUB NEWS | Supporters encouraged to arrive early for Joey Jones tribute ahead of FA Cup tie
item.description: Supporters of both sides are encouraged to take their seats early ahead of our FA Cup tie against Chelsea FC, with a tribute to Club icon Joey Jones set to take place before kick-off. A mosaic of cards has been designed to be raised from the Macron stand, ahead of the players walking out from the tunnel for the fixture. ‘Sir’ Joey Jones, a former Wales international and European champion, represented Wrexham across three spells with the Club, before a long association with the Club off the pitch
